Increasingly, most original equipment manufacturers now provide factory-tested, IEEE Std 1547-compliant BESS models that are ready for integration with simulation platforms. These models reflect current grid support functions—including ride-through, voltage and frequency regulation, and advanced controls—ensuring alignment with utility interconnection requirements. 3.6.2 Additional Model Requirements Custom development might still be required to: • Implement advanced control strategies tailored for data center microgrids and integrate with other backup assets, such as UPS and generators. • Support parallel operation and coordinated dispatch, unique to large-scale deployments. • Enable hardware-in-the-loop or real-time simulation for the comprehensive validation of BESS performance within complex, fast-varying data center loads. 3.7 Generator Models Generator models should incorporate the following key elements: • Startup delays and ramp rates—reflecting the response times of diesel, natural gas, or other backup generation asset • Load acceptance dynamics—capturing realistic backup power connection times during transitions • Protective relays—including maintain system frequency and overall power balance across multiple generators • Automatic voltage regulation—to control excitation and regulate voltage stability and reactive power output at the POI • Control modes: Isochronous control for maintaining constant frequency/speed, critical during o islanded or isolated operation Droop control for proportional load sharing among multiple parallel generators in o response to frequency changes Load-sharing schemes coordinating power dispatch among generators based on o capacity and system demands. 3.7.1 Standard PSCAD Models Available PSCAD offers detailed synchronous and asynchronous generator models, including excitation systems, governors, and protection schemes; however, these models are often challenging to integrate because the detailed dynamic characteristics and control parameters are typically not provided by manufacturers, making it difficult to accurately represent actual generator behavior. 3.7.2 Additional Model Requirements Custom development is needed to: • Capture real-world generator dynamics reflecting site-specific configurations and unique backup power operations. • Integrate tightly with UPS and BESS models for coordinated backup power responses under fault and transient conditions. • Include advanced control schemes allowing smooth switching between control modes (e.g., from droop to isochronous) depending on the operational scenarios. • Model fault ride-through capabilities and grid code compliance for reliable operation during disturbances. • Enable the simulation of coordinated load sharing and fault response among multiple generators to avoid overload and ensure stable power delivery. 3.8 Protection Systems Every breaker in the modeled system is assumed to have its own programmable thresholds. These thresholds define whether a specific subsystem remains connected or is isolated during an abnormal condition. Accurate protection system modeling requires: • Implementation of protective relay logic with customizable thresholds for voltage, current, and frequency
